neighbours.label: context where a right, privilege or possession is about to be taken away (revoked, lost, stripped); fires before/at the loss word
fire: If you are caught driving drunk again, your license will be revoked for a year.
Kids who break the house rules get their phone privileges taken away.
Doctors found guilty of fraud can lose their medical license permanently.
The new law would let the state strip citizenship from convicted spies.
Students caught cheating will automatically forfeit their scholarship funding.
After she missed curfew, her driving privileges were suspended for a month.
Protesters warned that the bill would take voting rights away from millions.
Members who don't pay by June will have their membership cancelled.
quiet: If you pass the safety course this spring, the state renews your license for a year.
Kids who follow the house rules earn extra screen time on weekends.
Doctors who finish the residency can apply for a medical license next year.
The new law would let the state grant citizenship to long-term residents.
Students with top grades will receive additional scholarship funding.
After she turned eighteen, her parents bought her a used car.
Protesters argued that the bill would expand voting access for millions.
Members who pay by June will get a ten percent discount.

notes: Top examples: license temporarily suspended, privilege is lost, grant money cut off, taken away; output promotes revoke/lose/stripped/loss.
